I recently watched 'The Pursuit of Happyness', with Will Smith and his son Jaden.
It's based on a true story, about a salesman who loses everything, and at one point he's sleeping in a train station bathroom with his little boy.
I'd heard it had a really inspiring message, and I'm a Will Smith fan anyway, so one weekend I finally sat down and watched it.
There's a scene where he tells his son, don't ever let somebody tell you you can't do something. That line stayed with me for days.
And honestly, the whole film made me think about how much I take for granted.
I've recently gotten into gardening.
It started when I found my grandmother's old gardening book in the attic. I got curious, bought some seeds, and just tried.
The first month was a disaster. I overwatered everything and my tomatoes died in two weeks.
But slowly I figured it out, and now I've got a small balcony garden. Chillies, mint, a few marigolds.
It's a little morning ritual now. Ten quiet minutes before the day starts, before the phone starts ringing.
